authority: CEO Round 149 — multi-part directive: attack C2 rescue, test common-mode cancellation, generate new invention hypotheses, rank globally

part_1_C2_rescue_attack.description: Separate the two rescue mechanisms and test each independently.

H_C2_R1.name: PHYSIOLOGICAL_DIFFERENTIAL_MECHANISM
H_C2_R1.description: C2 works because the eShunt-accessible venous compartment is sufficiently decoupled from CSF during the relevant pathological state. The differential carries independent physiological information.
H_C2_R1.test: Run the 26 winning regimes with sensor_mismatch=0 (no sensor bias difference). If advantage persists → H-C2-R1 supported. If advantage disappears → H-C2-R2 (cancellation) is the real mechanism.
H_C2_R1.expected_result_if_R1: Advantage persists with zero sensor mismatch → physiological decoupling is real
H_C2_R1.expected_result_if_R2: Advantage disappears with zero sensor mismatch → cancellation is the real mechanism

H_C2_R2.name: COMMON_MODE_CANCELLATION_MECHANISM
H_C2_R2.description: C2 works because subtracting two correlated sensors removes shared bias/drift/noise and improves classification. The advantage is signal-processing, not physiology.
H_C2_R2.test: Compare: (A) absolute ICP with single-sensor drift, (B) differential with two-sensor drift cancellation, (C) absolute ICP with drift compensation algorithm. If B ≈ C > A → cancellation is the mechanism, and it can be achieved without differential hardware.
H_C2_R2.expected_result_if_R2: Differential advantage ≈ drift-compensated absolute → the 'invention' is drift compensation, not differential sensing

local_perturbation_search.description: Perturb the 26 winning regimes to determine robustness.
local_perturbation_search.method: For each winning regime, perturb each parameter by ±20% and check if ΔAUROC > 0.05 persists.

part_2_new_invention_hypotheses.description: Generate successor hypotheses from C1/C2/C5 failure analyses. Per CEO: 'The cemetery should generate the next wave of hypotheses. But every successor begins at zero evidence.'

hypotheses.name: Predictive Shunt Failure Engine
hypotheses.concept: Predict degradation before complete failure and classify the likely failure mode using longitudinal pressure-flow dynamics.
hypotheses.moat: Patient-specific state model + longitudinal calibration + failure prediction + failure-mode classification
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: MODERATE — US20060047201A1 teaches temporal processing for shunt malfunction. But failure-mode CLASSIFICATION (obstruction vs overdrainage vs fracture vs migration) + PREDICTION (before failure) may be novel.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Can longitudinal physiological response distinguish obstruction from overdrainage from underdrainage from valve dysfunction from catheter fracture from migration, AND predict failure before clinical symptoms?
hypotheses.falsifiability: HIGH — can be tested with virtual cohort simulation
hypotheses.strategic_value: HIGH — converts device into intelligent system
hypotheses.IP_defensibility: MODERATE — the decision policy is harder to design around than a sensor
hypotheses.difficulty_to_design_around: HIGH — requires longitudinal data + validated model
hypotheses.validation_cost: MEDIUM — virtual cohort + eventual clinical data
hypotheses.ranking_score: TBD — needs prior-art search + scientific test

hypotheses.name: Closed-Loop Adaptive Drainage
hypotheses.concept: System estimates physiological state and continuously adapts drainage behavior toward patient-specific target manifold.
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: HIGH — adjustable valves exist (WO2020086847A1 teaches P_CSF feedback control). Adaptive control may be obvious over fixed control.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Can an adaptive controller produce materially better physiological trajectory than fixed drainage without unacceptable instability?
hypotheses.IP_defensibility: MODERATE — control policy may be patentable but hard to enforce
hypotheses.validation_cost: HIGH — requires control system engineering + safety analysis

hypotheses.name: CSF Dynamics Fingerprint
hypotheses.concept: Patient-specific pressure dynamics represented as a persistent physiological fingerprint distinguishing normal from evolving device/pathology states.
hypotheses.moat: Temporal state model + patient-specific baseline + longitudinal deviation detection
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: HIGH — US20060047201A1 teaches temporal processing. 2025 Neurology study shows waveform analysis. The 'fingerprint' concept may be obvious over known waveform analysis.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Can patient-specific pressure dynamics be represented as a fingerprint that provides information beyond known waveform features (P2/P1, time-to-peak)?
hypotheses.strategic_value: MEDIUM — useful but may be hard to differentiate from prior art
hypotheses.IP_defensibility: LOW-MODERATE — if prior art teaches temporal analysis, fingerprint is a natural extension

hypotheses.name: Physiological Perturbation Identification
hypotheses.concept: Apply safe controlled perturbation (postural transition, valve state change) and infer CSF hydraulic system parameters from the response.
hypotheses.moat: System identification methodology + parameter estimation + diagnostic inference
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: LOW-MODERATE — active perturbation for diagnosis is less common than passive monitoring. System identification in CSF context may be novel.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Does active perturbation produce information that passive observation cannot? Can system parameters (R_shunt, C_brain, valve_state) be estimated from perturbation response?
hypotheses.falsifiability: VERY HIGH — clearly testable with virtual cohort
hypotheses.strategic_value: HIGH — converts passive monitoring into active diagnosis
hypotheses.IP_defensibility: HIGH — system identification methodology is harder to design around than a sensor
hypotheses.difficulty_to_design_around: HIGH — requires validated perturbation protocol + parameter estimation + clinical interpretation
hypotheses.validation_cost: MEDIUM — virtual cohort + eventual clinical protocol

hypotheses.name: Predictive Embolic-Risk Engine
hypotheses.concept: Estimate fragmentation probability and time-to-fragmentation before the event, extending beyond single-precursor detection.
hypotheses.moat: Physics-based model + patient-specific twin + validated prediction across independent worlds
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: LOW — embolic-risk prediction from clot mechanics is not well-established in prior art. The C5 precursor work (even if custom-world-only) establishes a novel computational approach.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Does a physically measurable precursor consistently predict fragmentation across independent models AND across clot geometries, material properties, and flow conditions?
hypotheses.falsifiability: VERY HIGH — directly testable with multi-world simulation
hypotheses.strategic_value: VERY HIGH — extends beyond eShunt to all thrombectomy procedures
hypotheses.IP_defensibility: HIGH — physics-based prediction model is harder to design around than a sensor
hypotheses.difficulty_to_design_around: HIGH — requires validated computational model + multi-world evidence
hypotheses.validation_cost: HIGH — requires external clotFoam + Peridigm + virtual cohort

hypotheses.name: Intervention Optimizer
hypotheses.concept: If predictive precursor survives, use the model to choose interventions that minimize fragmentation/embolization risk.
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: LOW — intervention optimization for thrombectomy is not well-established
hypotheses.scientific_question: Can the model compare candidate interventions (flow rate, catheter position, aspiration strategy) and predict which minimizes embolization risk?
hypotheses.falsifiability: HIGH — testable with virtual intervention comparison
hypotheses.strategic_value: VERY HIGH — transforms prediction into decision support
hypotheses.validation_cost: HIGH — requires C5-X to succeed first

hypotheses.name: Closed-Loop CNS Delivery
hypotheses.concept: Sense → infer → decide → deliver → monitor → learn. C3 becomes the therapeutic arm of the platform.
hypotheses.moat: Closed-loop drug delivery + physiological feedback + longitudinal optimization
hypotheses.prior_art_risk: MODERATE — closed-loop insulin delivery exists (artificial pancreas). CNS closed-loop delivery is less established.
hypotheses.scientific_question: Can physiological feedback (CSF pressure, biomarkers) optimize CNS drug delivery in real-time?
hypotheses.validation_cost: VERY HIGH — requires drug delivery + sensor + controller + clinical validation

part_3_global_ranking.formula: technical_novelty × scientific_falsifiability × strategic_value × IP_defensibility × difficulty_to_design_around ÷ validation_cost

initial_ranking.rationale: Highest strategic value (extends beyond eShunt), low prior-art risk, very high falsifiability, very high IP defensibility. Depends on C5 external clotFoam resolution. VALIDATION_COST is high but justifiable.
Novel concept (active perturbation for system ID), low-moderate prior-art risk, very high falsifiability, high IP defensibility. Can be tested immediately with virtual cohort.
High strategic value, moderate prior-art risk, high falsifiability. Failure-mode classification + prediction is commercially compelling.
Very high strategic value but depends on C5-X success. Cannot be independently tested until C5-X is validated.
High strategic value but very high validation cost. Closed-loop CNS delivery is ambitious.
High prior-art risk (US20060047201A1 + 2025 waveform literature). 'Fingerprint' may be obvious over known waveform analysis.
High prior-art risk (adjustable valves exist). Adaptive control may be obvious. High validation cost.

part_4_c2_rescue_verdict.rationale: Round 148 found 26 winning regimes but the mechanism is unclear. Two hypotheses (physiological vs cancellation) must be separated. If the advantage is purely sensor-mismatch cancellation, the 'invention' is drift compensation, not differential sensing. This would be a different invention (C2-R2) with different prior-art implications.
part_4_c2_rescue_verdict.next_action: Run the H-C2-R1 vs H-C2-R2 separation test: set sensor_mismatch=0 in the 26 winning regimes and check if advantage persists.

part_5_portfolio_status.summary: 7 new invention hypotheses generated from failure analyses. Ranked globally. C5-X and C2-Y are highest-priority new candidates. C2 rescue mechanism must be separated before C2 can advance or die.
